text:
The trembling patriarch shook the universe.
Isis, the Mother, at last rose from her bed,
gave her savage husband a look of hatred,
and the old ardor blazed in her green eyes.

“Look at him,” she says, “that wicked old man sleeps;
all the world’s ice has passed through his mouth.
Beware his foot; put out his crooked eye:
he is king of volcanoes, god of winters.”

“The eagle has passed: Napoleon calls me;
for him I have donned Cybele’s mantle.
I am Hermes’ wife, Osiris’ sister…”

The goddess had escaped in her golden shell;
the sea returned her worshiped image to us,
and the skies shone beneath Iris’ scarf.

translation.title: To Luisa D’Or, Queen
translation.editorial_note: Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
